#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Don't update `client-affinity lists` for not ready endpoint to let the fault endpoints cannot be isolate appropriately:

1. When a client accesses a session affinity service, the `client-affinity lists` is updated each time the client accesses the service to maintain the session affinity.
2. If the endpoint is faulty, as long as the client keeps trying to access the service, the `client-affinity lists` is updated and the session affinity is maintained. As a result, the faulty endpoint cannot be isolated.
3. Therefore, kube-proxy shouldn't renew `client-affinity lists`(in iptables proxy mode that is `iptables recent record`) for not ready endpoint. In this way, when maximum session sticky time has been exceeded, traffic can be switched to other normal endpoints.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:
<!--

-->
Fixes [#110302](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/110302)

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

1、I'm not sure if this change will result in a user-facing change
2、This modification only considers the scenario where proxy-mode is iptables. I don't know exactly what these behaviors are like in ipvs mode.

issue_context.title: Service with session affinity cannot isolate the fault appropriately
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

By setting service.spec.sessionAffinity to "ClientIP", connections from a particular client are passed to the same Pod each time when accessing a Service.
When the Pod that the client continuously accesses becomes not ready, the client will still access the NotReady Pod because of the iptables rules, even if the maximum session sticky time has been exceeded, which caused the request of the client cannot be passed to the ready Pod.

### What did you expect to happen?

Service with session affinity can isolate the fault appropriately, after the maximum session sticky time, traffic can be redirected to one of the ready Pods.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. kube-proxy runnnig with iptables proxy mode
2. create a session affinity Service with two endpoints
3. make a client accesses the Service periodically
4. stop one of the endpoints(the client accesses) and make it not ready
5. the client  accesses the notready endpoint periodically

### Anything else we need to know?

kube-proxy runnnig with iptables proxy mode in my cluster.

In this case it sounds like your client has an open connection, right (as opposed to closing it and periodically re-opening)?  Or am I misunderstanding?  If so, this is about connection tracking, not affinity.

Session affinity only matters for new connections, not new packets on existing connections.  In (almost?) every implementation, kube-proxy is more of a router than a proxy, which means your client pod is connected to the server directly, with some address translation in between.  

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/108523#issuecomment-1071832988

I think that it is correct to leave open sessions to not-ready endpoints - this is important for gracefully draining traffic when things like deployment updates are happening.

If you need your clients to disconnect, you have to do that yourself from within the server.
